title: Harden developer tooling to fail closed and verify postconditions
description:
## Summary
The 2026-09-12 engineering/security/tooling audit found no critical application-security defect, but identified that repository tooling is treated as disposable scaffolding rather than as a controlled part of the engineering system: scripts do not declare local-versus-repository state, deployment verifies exit codes but not artifacts, and there is no repository-wide secret-scan rule.

## User Mandate
> "As always, look for recurring issues and patterns of bugs or mistakes that we can add process safeguards against"

STRICT. This task exists to add process safeguards against recurring tooling failure modes. Do not relax, re-scope, or silently drop any safeguard listed in Scope.

## Scope
- ET-01: document a repository-wide secret rule (no tokens, cookies, auth-bearing MCP endpoints, or exported connection files) and define a lightweight local scan step.
- ET-02/ET-05: deployment scripts must verify postconditions (output path and expected files exist; service responds) instead of trusting `$LASTEXITCODE`; document which scripts support a dry run.
- ET-04/ET-09: classify every artifact as source-of-truth, generated-but-committed, generated-and-ignored, or local-only, and reflect that in `.gitignore` and the README.
- ET-03/ET-08: document the task-import tooling as strictly one-way and resumable; fail closed when configuration is missing.
- Meta-synthesis item: any new validation/normalization script must report its own inability to process an input as a failure, not a silent skip.
- Out of scope: recreating CI (TSK-0123, Rejected).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A documented artifact-classification table exists and matches `.gitignore`.
- `Deploy-CreatureWiki.ps1` and `Bootstrap-CreatureWikiEngine.ps1` verify at least one concrete postcondition beyond exit code, or record an explicit justification for not doing so.
- A dry-run or explicit "no dry-run" statement exists for each script that mutates local state.
- The secret rule is documented and a repeatable local scan command is defined.
- `Import-CreatureTasksToMemorySmith.ps1` is documented as one-way with its dry-run contract stated.

## Validation
- Re-read each script after edit; confirm the postcondition check and dry-run statement.
- Run the documented local scan command and record its output.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- No runtime code change, so no Unity gate is required for this task.

## Findings
- Verified: `Bootstrap-CreatureWikiEngine.ps1` and `Deploy-CreatureWiki.ps1` do check `$LASTEXITCODE` and throw on failure. The residual gap is postcondition verification, not exit-code handling.
- Verified: `Import-CreatureTasksToMemorySmith.ps1` already implements `-DryRun`; the deploy path does not.
- Verified: `.gitignore` protects the credential-bearing `.vscode/mcp.json`.
- Caveat: the audit's "scripts have effects larger than their documentation" claim is partially refuted — exit-code gating is present.

## Blockers
- None. All items are source- and tooling-verifiable without Unity.

## Next Step
Add postcondition checks to the two deploy/bootstrap scripts, then write the artifact-classification table into the README and align `.gitignore`.
